title: SC1d test asserts only in-memory task status, not the durable lifecycle.crashed event — replay contract untested
claim: The SC1d test ('a refused adapter spawn fails the task') asserts only `r.status === 'failed'`, which reads the in-memory `task.status` set directly at coordinator.mjs:253. It never asserts the `lifecycle.crashed` (payload.phase:'spawn') log event appended at coordinator.mjs:244-251, even though the implementation comment and spec justify the design by 'replay already folds it to failed'. No other test in the suite pins this event (grep for 'crashed'/'_onSpawnRefused' across coordinator.test.mjs, phase8-correctness.test.mjs, e2e.test.mjs finds nothing for this producer).
evidence: impl/test/phase10-completion.test.mjs:198-205 (only assertion is on r.status); impl/src/coordinator.mjs:242-255 (_onSpawnRefused appends lifecycle.crashed AND sets task.status independently); impl/src/coordinator.mjs:944-961 (_replay derives 'failed' only from the logged lifecycle.crashed/forced_stop kinds; spawned+turn_started alone replays to 'working')
failureScenario: Regression deletes (or typos the kind of) the `this._log.append({... kind: 'lifecycle.crashed', payload: {phase: 'spawn'} ...})` call in _onSpawnRefused while keeping `task.status = 'failed'`. All 411 tests stay green (SC1d passes on the in-memory status). A coordinator restart then replays a log containing only lifecycle.spawned + lifecycle.turn_started for the refused-spawn worker, and _replay() rebuilds the task as status 'working' with a 'working' handle — the exact zombie-stuck-in-working failure mode SC1d exists to kill, resurrected across every restart, and invisible to the story compiler.

title: GLM env-probe tests can print a REAL ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN in test output on their failure path
claim: The env-threading tests spawn fake-claude with the child env built as `{ ...process.env, ...(this._cfg.env ?? {}) }` (claude-session.mjs:152) and assert on the child-echoed value with failure messages that interpolate it verbatim (`child reported: ${done.payload.result.summary}` at lines 123 and 157). saveEnv (line 106/147) clears only Z_AI_API_KEY/ZHIPU_API_KEY — it never clears an inherited real ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN from the developer/CI shell. fake-claude's REPORT_ENV marker echoes whatever the child actually received (fixtures/fake-claude.mjs:205-213). This violates the file's own stated discipline ('values are never printed/logged', line 9-10) precisely when the test fires.
evidence: impl/test/glm-session.test.mjs:104-128 (probe g2 'REPORT_ENV:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN' at line 114, interpolating assertion at line 123), :145-159 (same pattern at line 157), :62-71 (saveEnv covers only Z_AI_API_KEY/ZHIPU_API_KEY); impl/src/claude-session.mjs:152 (child inherits full process.env); impl/test/fixtures/fake-claude.mjs:205-213 (REPORT_ENV echoes any received value)
failureScenario: A machine running the suite has a real ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN exported (routine for Claude Code users / CI). A regression breaks GLM env threading — e.g. claude-session's spread order flips to `{...cfg.env, ...process.env}`, or GlmSessionCli's env option is renamed — so the child inherits the REAL token instead of the fake override. The test correctly fails, but its assertion message prints `child reported: env:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<real secret>` into the test/CI log, leaking a live credential exactly when the test does its job. Fix: add ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) to saveEnv+delete, and/or redact the reported value for the AUTH_TOKEN probe's diagnostic.

title: Claude driver-e2e tests carry no cwd proof — a wrong-cwd claude worker passes both SC3 driver tests
claim: The commit message claims 'cwd-echo proves each worker ran IN its task worktree' for the SC3/SC10 driver tier, but only the codex (line 124-128) and grok (line 142-144) driver tests assert a cwd echo. Both claude driver tests use HOLD_UNTIL_INTERRUPT and assert only turn_started/steer-ok/completed/verdict.reverified and cancelled — none of which depend on where the child ran. Claude's cwd proof exists only at adapter level (SC1a, phase10-completion.test.mjs:137-150), which passes bare `{worktreeReady}` and never sees the coordinator's actual opts shape `{worktreeReady, timeoutMs}` (coordinator.mjs:225-227).
evidence: impl/test/phase10-driver-e2e.test.mjs:88-112 (no cwd assertion in either claude test); impl/src/coordinator.mjs:225-227 (dispatch passes {worktreeReady, timeoutMs}); impl/test/phase10-completion.test.mjs:142 (SC1a passes {worktreeReady} only)
failureScenario: A future claude-session spawn refactor mishandles cwd only under the coordinator's opts shape (e.g. an opts-normalization rewrite that resolves worktreeReady for the refusal check but drops the resolved path when timeoutMs is also present), spawning the claude child in the orchestrator cwd. SC1a stays green (different opts shape), both claude driver tests stay green (task 'completes' — the trust gate runs `true` in its own fresh sandbox regardless of where the worker ran), and the G1 silent-wrong-cwd failure ships for the claude vendor while codex/grok would have been caught by their echoes. One extra spawn of goal 'REPORT_CWD' through the driver with the existing waitForLogEvent cwd-echo pattern closes it.

title: SC8 session-card rows check shape only; the claimed 'values pinned by their own suites' backstop has holes (claude pause, codex answer/kill)
claim: For the three session adapters, CARD_CASES sets expected=null (lines 412-414), so the SC8 test asserts only the 8-key shape and closed-set membership — any of native/emulated/unsupported passes for every verb. The justifying comment says values are 'pinned by their own suites', but claude-session.test.mjs pins 7 of 8 verbs (pause is never asserted) and codex-appserver.test.mjs pins 6 of 8 (answer and kill are never asserted); only grok-acp.test.mjs pins all 8.
evidence: impl/test/phase10-completion.test.mjs:411-414, 427-429 (expected=null skips the value deepEqual); impl/test/claude-session.test.mjs:115-131 (no verbs.pause assertion); impl/test/codex-appserver.test.mjs:113-118 (no verbs.answer or verbs.kill assertion)
failureScenario: ClaudeSessionCli.card() is edited to claim pause:'native' (no pause method exists), or CodexAppServerCli.card() drifts answer to 'native' without an implementation. All 411 tests stay green — 'native' is inside the closed set and the vendor suites never touch those keys — so a fleet operator's card claims a verb its adapter stubs out: the exact docs/22 overclaim pattern SC8 states it exists to prevent ('values honest to the implemented surface').

title: kill()/interrupt() during spawn's worktreeReady await is a silent no-op; the vendor child is created afterward and becomes a permanently unkillable orphan
claim: SC1 moved `await opts.worktreeReady` inside all three session adapters' spawn() BEFORE the child process exists and before any session is registered in _sessions (claude-session.mjs:130-136 -> child at 150; codex-appserver.mjs:382-389 -> child at 391; grok-acp.mjs:408-415 -> child at 417). Every adapter's kill() no-ops when no session is registered (claude-session.mjs:449-450 `if (!session || session.terminal) return { ok: true }`; codex-appserver.mjs:579-580; grok-acp.mjs:572-573), and nothing records the stop for the still-awaiting spawn to observe. So a stop issued while worktree creation is in flight neither prevents nor ever reaches the child that spawn() goes on to create.
evidence: claude-session.mjs:130-136,150,449-450; codex-appserver.mjs:382-391,579-580; grok-acp.mjs:408-417,572-573; coordinator.mjs:210-215 (worktreeReady pending at dispatch), 505 (stop-deadline timer), 577-601 (_forceStop: status 'dead', task 'failed', adapter.kill no-op, waiter deleted), 453-454 (kill() short-circuits `already_dead` for status 'dead'), 782 (turn_completed for a 'dead' handle: trust gate skipped, no kill issued). No test exercises a stop while worktreeReady is pending — all SC1 tests pass pre-resolved promises (phase10-completion.test.mjs:142,167,177,190).
failureScenario: Task dispatched; _worktrees.create(taskId) is slow (large repo / slow disk). Coordinator.kill(workerId) arrives during the window: adapter.kill finds no session, returns {ok:true}; kill.confirmed never comes; stop-deadline fires _forceStop -> handle 'dead', task 'failed', worktree removal racing the pending create, waiter deleted. worktreeReady then resolves -> spawn() proceeds and launches a REAL vendor CLI (Claude Code with --permission-mode acceptEdits) which runs the full brief unsupervised, spending real subscription/API budget and editing disk. The coordinator will never kill it: turn events are logged but the gate is skipped, and a second kill(workerId) short-circuits with 'already_dead' (coordinator.mjs:454). The orphan is invisible (task reads failed, phase:'spawn' never logged) and unkillable through the API.

title: _deliver's slot-acquisition guard only checks 'stopping': a queued send delivers after the stop completes — resurrecting a cancelled task or claiming ok:true delivery to a dead worker
claim: SC4b's revalidation at slot acquisition re-checks only `handle.status === 'stopping'` (coordinator.mjs:387). interrupt()/kill() bypass the sendChain (by design), so a stop requested AFTER a send was queued can fully finalize before the queued send's slot opens, leaving status 'idle' (interrupt confirmed, _finalizeStop:566) or 'dead' (kill confirmed / _forceStop:590) — both of which pass the guard. The fence gives no protection either: _fences.issue() at delivery (409) returns the CURRENT stamp, i.e. post-bumpHuman, so the interrupt's human bump can never stale-reject an already-queued send; and the adapter's prompt ack.ok is never consulted (409, 438), so a refused delivery still logs control.send/control.steer and returns {ok:true}. The SC4b test (coordinator.test.mjs:503) deliberately avoids awaiting the interrupt precisely because 'the worker would no longer be stopping by the time B's slot opened' — the untested post-stop states are exactly the hole.
evidence: coordinator.mjs:380-383 (chain), 385-387 (guard), 407-409 (issue after bumpHuman at 481; ack unchecked), 434-438 (control.send logged + ok:true regardless of ack.ok), 546-575 (_finalizeStop -> 'idle', task 'cancelled'), 577-601 (_forceStop -> 'dead'), 777-785 (turn_completed from 'idle' handle runs the trust gate; TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES:43 does not include 'cancelled'); claude-session.mjs:343-365 (prompt only rejects terminal sessions; a mid-grace _forceStop-killed child still accepts the frame and emits lifecycle.turn_started); phase10-completion.test.mjs:231-256 (only the still-'stopping' case is pinned).
failureScenario: send#1 in flight (slow adapter.prompt); operator queues send#2, then calls interrupt(w) which confirms natively (status 'working'->'stopping'->'idle', task 'cancelled', fence bumped). send#1 settles; send#2's _deliver runs: status 'idle' passes the guard, issue() returns the post-bump stamp so the fence check passes, the adapter starts a WHOLE NEW TURN on the cancelled task, control.send is logged ok, and on turn_completed the trust gate flips the task 'cancelled' -> 'verifying' -> 'completed' — the operator's interrupt is silently undone by a send issued BEFORE it. Kill variant: after kill.confirmed or _forceStop (status 'dead'), the queued send still delivers — coordinator returns {ok:true, result:'ok'} for a message the adapter refused ({ok:false, 'unknown or terminal worker'}) and appends control.send AFTER kill.confirmed/control.forced_stop; in the _forceStop+claude killGraceMs window the frame actually reaches the dying child and emits lifecycle.turn_started post-forced_stop (story: illegal_transition warning, dead worker 'resurrects' in the log).

title: codex turn/start failure refuses the spawn but leaks a live app-server child and a non-terminal session — SC1d marks the task failed while a real process (possibly a running turn) survives
claim: CodexAppServerCli.spawn()'s initialize and thread/start failure paths call _killChild + _sessions.delete before refusing, but the turn/start failure path (codex-appserver.mjs:441-449) returns {ok:false} WITHOUT killing the child or deleting the session. The new SC1d consumer (_onSpawnRefused, coordinator.mjs:242-255) treats every refusal as terminal — logs lifecycle.crashed phase:'spawn', sets handle 'exited', task 'failed' — but never issues adapter.kill, on the (now false) assumption that a refused spawn left nothing running. Before this commit the refusal ack was discarded entirely, so this seam is newly load-bearing.
evidence: codex-appserver.mjs:412-418 and 429-435 (failure paths that DO tear down) vs 441-449 (turn/start catch: bare return, child alive, session in _sessions with terminal:false); coordinator.mjs:225-230 (ack consumed), 242-255 (_onSpawnRefused: no adapter.kill, no worktree removal); phase10 tests only cover refusals at the cwd stage (phase10-completion.test.mjs:152-170), never a post-handshake refusal.
failureScenario: initialize and thread/start succeed against a live codex app-server; turn/start times out (requestTimeoutMs) or errors after the request was actually delivered. spawn resolves {ok:false} -> coordinator fails the task and marks the worker exited, but the app-server child — which may have genuinely started the turn (the response, not the request, was lost) — keeps running in the task worktree indefinitely: an agent actively editing files for a task the coordinator reports as failed, with no automatic teardown (kill is only ever triggered by stop waiters, and none exists).

title: Session adapters ignore opts.timeoutMs — the wallMin budget the coordinator passes at dispatch is silently unenforced on the entire session tier
claim: _dispatch passes `timeoutMs: wallMin * 60000` into adapter.spawn opts (coordinator.mjs:225-228) and relies on the adapter to enforce it — the subprocess tier does (cli-adapters.mjs:151 arms a SIGKILL timer). None of the three session adapters (ClaudeSessionCli, CodexAppServerCli, GrokAcpCli) read opts.timeoutMs at all, and the coordinator has no other wall-clock sweep for working tasks (_sweepDeadlines covers only approvals and stop waiters). SC1 is what first made coordinator->session-adapter dispatch functional, so the drop is newly reachable: the tier this commit ships as the product surface loses the only wall-clock budget mechanism.
evidence: coordinator.mjs:222-228; cli-adapters.mjs:151 (the only opts.timeoutMs consumer in impl/src); no occurrence of timeoutMs-from-opts in claude-session.mjs, codex-appserver.mjs (only _requestTimeoutMs for RPCs), or grok-acp.mjs; coordinator.mjs:161-173 (_sweepDeadlines: approvals + stop waiters only).
failureScenario: A task with brief.budget.wallMin=5 dispatched to ClaudeSessionCli enters a runaway turn (agent loops on a failing build). The subprocess tier would SIGKILL at 5 minutes; the session tier never does — the worker runs unbounded, consuming budget until a human notices, while list()/story report an ordinary 'working' worker.

title: _onSpawnRefused's dedup guard checks a status ('exited') no other coordinator path ever sets, and it overwrites terminal state unconditionally
claim: _onSpawnRefused skips only when `handle.status === 'exited'` (coordinator.mjs:243), documented as 'skipped if an adapter event already ended the worker'. But the adapter-crash path sets 'idle' (792) and the stop paths set 'dead' (590) or 'idle' (566) — 'exited' is set nowhere except by _onSpawnRefused itself, so the intended crash-vs-refusal dedup can never fire, and the function unconditionally overwrites handle.status ('dead' -> 'exited') and task.status ('failed', with no TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES guard, unlike the crash handler at 791).
evidence: coordinator.mjs:242-255 vs 787-793 (lifecycle.crashed handler sets 'idle', guards terminal task statuses) and 589-592 (_forceStop sets 'dead'); grep confirms 'exited' appears in coordinator.mjs only inside _onSpawnRefused.
failureScenario: Worktree creation fails (worktreeReady resolves null) while the operator kills the worker: adapter.kill no-ops (no session yet), _forceStop fires -> handle 'dead', task 'failed', control.forced_stop logged, kill() now short-circuits 'already_dead'. The refusal ack then arrives: guard sees 'dead' != 'exited', so a SECOND terminal lifecycle event (lifecycle.crashed phase:'spawn') is appended after control.forced_stop and handle.status regresses 'dead' -> 'exited', after which kill(workerId) no longer short-circuits as already_dead — the worker's terminal accounting (log and handle) is duplicated and inconsistent.

title: SC5d: 'non-crashed exited' is proxied by unrelated warning signals — crashed workers count as done; clean exits with budget warnings are dropped from doneCount
claim: SC5d requires doneCount to count 'non-crashed exited workers plus workers whose lastVerdict.accept === true', but the implementation determines 'non-crashed' via hasCrashWarning(), which inspects only stalled/looping/over_budget/out_of_scope signals (story.mjs:611-614, 644-646) and cannot detect crashes at all, because the fold collapses both KIND.EXITED and KIND.CRASHED to the same status 'exited' with no crash marker on the worker story (story.mjs:338-341). The proxy is wrong in both directions.
evidence: story.mjs:621-623 (doneCount filter), story.mjs:644-646 (hasCrashWarning checks Array length of stalled/looping/over_budget/out_of_scope signals only — see the filter at story.mjs:612), story.mjs:338-341 (EXITED and CRASHED both fold to w.status='exited' indistinguishably), story.mjs:554 (STATUS_PHRASE.exited renders 'done'). Runtime-confirmed: folding spawned→turn_started→lifecycle.crashed renders '0 worker(s) active, 1 done' with line 'w1 (t1): done'; folding spawned→turn_started→resource.tokens(60% of budget)→turn_completed→lifecycle.exited(code 0) renders '0 worker(s) active' (no done count) while the same output's worker line says 'done — 50% budget'.
failureScenario: Direction 1: a worker crashes (adapter emits lifecycle.crashed, e.g. claude child exits nonzero, claude-session.mjs:477). The story folds it to status 'exited' with no stall/loop/budget/scope signal, so hasCrashWarning is false and the narrative reports '0 worker(s) active, 1 done' with the worker line reading 'done' — a crashed task presented to the operator as completed work, the exact story-untruth SC5 exists to close. (Same for a killed/cancelled worker via SC5a's kill.confirmed→exited fold: it also renders '1 done'.) Direction 2: a worker cleanly completes and exits after using 60% of its token budget; the persistent over_budget threshold signal makes hasCrashWarning true, so the header omits it from doneCount while its own line simultaneously says 'done — 50% budget' — the header and the body contradict each other. The new SC5d tests only cover the idle+lastVerdict paths, so 411/411 stays green.

title: SC1d half-implemented: a spawn() that REJECTS (rather than resolving {ok:false}) is still swallowed by .catch(noop) — the zombie stuck-in-'working' task the contract exists to eliminate
claim: SC1d's purpose is 'a refused spawn... never a zombie stuck in working' (spec rationale: 'Today a refused spawn leaves a zombie task in working forever'; commit message: 'never a zombie stuck in working'). The implementation consumes only a RESOLVED Ack with ok===false (coordinator.mjs:228-229); a spawn promise that rejects still hits .catch(noop) at coordinator.mjs:230 and is discarded, leaving task 'working' and handle 'working' forever with no lifecycle.crashed appended.
evidence: coordinator.mjs:225-230 (.then((ack) => { if (ack && ack.ok === false) this._onSpawnRefused(...) }).catch(noop)). Rejection paths exist in the shipped adapters: codex-appserver.mjs:391 and grok-acp.mjs:417 call this._spawnFn(...) with no try/catch (node's spawn throws synchronously on invalid cmd/args, e.g. cmd:'' → ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE), unlike claude-session.mjs:148-158 which wraps it; grok-acp.mjs:468 calls renderBrief(brief,'grok-acp') outside any try/catch, which throws on a brief lacking .verification (adapter.mjs:79). Runtime-confirmed with a real Coordinator and an adapter whose spawn rejects: after 100ms the task status is 'working' and the log contains only lifecycle.spawned,lifecycle.turn_started — the exact pre-SC1d zombie.
failureScenario: Operator misconfigures a session adapter (e.g. new GrokAcpCli({cmd:''}) or a plain-object brief missing verification passed straight to coordinator.spawn): dispatch fires, adapter.spawn throws/rejects before returning an Ack, .catch(noop) swallows it, and the task sits in 'working' forever — no lifecycle.crashed phase:'spawn', no 'failed' state, waitForAll never settles for it. The SC1d test only exercises a spawn resolving {ok:false, reason}, so the suite cannot catch the rejection path. Fix is one line: route the catch into _onSpawnRefused with a synthesized {ok:false, reason:String(err)} ack.

title: Codex wire-stage spawn refusal (turn/start failure) now fails the task but leaks a live app-server child that neither side ever kills
claim: CodexAppServerCli.spawn's turn/start failure path returns {ok:false} without _killChild(session) or this._sessions.delete(worker) (codex-appserver.mjs:446-448), unlike the initialize and thread/start failure paths directly above it (codex-appserver.mjs:414-417, 429-434) which both kill the child and delete the session. With SC1d the coordinator now consumes this refusal, marks the handle 'exited' and the task 'failed' — but never issues adapter.kill, so the fully-initialized app-server child stays alive indefinitely and the stale non-terminal session entry blocks the worker id in this._sessions.
evidence: codex-appserver.mjs:441-448 (catch returns ok:false with no cleanup, contrast :414-417 and :429-434); coordinator.mjs:242-255 (_onSpawnRefused sets statuses and appends lifecycle.crashed but performs no adapter cleanup); coordinator.mjs:451-455 (a later kill() would still reach _beginStop since the handle status is 'exited', not 'dead', but nothing in the SC1d path calls it).
failureScenario: A real codex app-server initializes and starts a thread in the task worktree, then turn/start fails (transient overload / invalid model arg). spawn resolves {ok:false}; SC1d fails the task — correct at the task layer — but the spawned app-server process keeps running until the orchestrator exits, accumulating one orphaned live child (holding the worktree cwd open) per occurrence in a long-running fleet. No test covers a turn/start-stage refusal, so the leak is invisible to the 411-green suite. Note the coordinator half of this is new in b85c58d ('exited' at coordinator.mjs:252 is also a status alien to the coordinator's own {pending,working,stopping,blocked,idle,dead} vocabulary, so the guard at :243 can never match a worker ended by adapter events, which set 'idle' or 'dead').

title: SC1d refusal handler clobbers a finalized kill: 'cancelled' task flips to 'failed' and a spurious lifecycle.crashed enters the log
claim: _onSpawnRefused guards only on handle.status === 'exited', a status no other coordinator path ever sets (kill finalization sets 'dead' at coordinator.mjs:560, crash/exit events set 'idle' at :792), so the guard never covers the adapter-event race it claims to; because 'cancelled' is not in TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES (coordinator.mjs:43), the handler then unconditionally rewrites a user-cancelled task to 'failed', appends a fabricated lifecycle.crashed AFTER kill.confirmed, and flips the handle from 'dead' to 'exited' (breaking kill()'s already_dead idempotency check at :454).
evidence: coordinator.mjs:243 (guard), :252-254 (unconditional handle='exited'/task='failed'), :43 (TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES lacks 'cancelled'), :559-567 (kill finalize sets 'cancelled'); grok-acp.mjs:201-215 (child close both emits kill.confirmed and rejects the pending handshake RPC, so the same close produces the confirm AND the refused spawn Ack), grok-acp.mjs:447-451; codex-appserver.mjs:412-418 has the identical structure. Empirically reproduced (scratch repro1b): trace shows append:kill.confirmed -> append:lifecycle.crashed, final task 'failed', handle 'exited'.
failureScenario: Operator calls coordinator.kill(w) while a grok/codex spawn handshake (initialize/session-new/thread-start) is in flight — the session is already in the adapter map, so adapter.kill SIGKILLs the child; the child's close handler emits kill.confirmed (stop finalizes: task 'cancelled', kill.confirmed logged) and rejects the pending handshake RPC, making spawn resolve {ok:false, reason:'stdio closed before responding'}; the SC1d .then then runs _onSpawnRefused, which logs lifecycle.crashed{phase:'spawn'} for a deliberate kill and rewrites the finalized task from 'cancelled' to 'failed'. result() reports 'failed' for a user cancellation, and D10 replay of the now-contradictory log (kill.confirmed followed by lifecycle.crashed) rebuilds 'failed' instead of 'cancelled'.

title: SC4 queued send outlives the stop window: delivered to a cancelled worker and the trust gate resurrects the cancelled task to 'completed'
claim: _deliver's slot-time guard checks only status === 'stopping'; a send queued behind an in-flight delivery while a stop is pending re-evaluates after _finalizeStop has moved the worker to 'idle' (interrupt) or 'dead' (kill), so it passes, is delivered to the adapter (returning {ok:true, result:'ok'} to the caller and logging control.send), starts a new turn on a task the user cancelled, and — since 'cancelled' is not in TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES — that turn's completion runs _runTrustGate, which rewrites the cancelled task to 'verifying' then 'completed'/'failed'. Pre-change, a send during 'stopping' deterministically returned {ok:false, result:'worker_stopping'}.
evidence: coordinator.mjs:380-382 (sendChain queue), :385-387 ('stopping'-only guard at slot acquisition), :565-567 (interrupt finalize -> handle 'idle', task 'cancelled'), :43 ('cancelled' non-terminal), :777-785 (turn_completed -> trust gate when not stopping/dead), :893 (task.status = accept ? 'completed' : 'failed'). The SC4b test (phase10-completion.test.mjs:244-246) deliberately keeps the stop pending, acknowledging in its comment that a finalized stop would let B through — the exact uncovered window. Empirically reproduced (scratch repro2): rB={ok:true,result:'ok'}, promptLog A,B, task 'cancelled' -> 'completed'.
failureScenario: Worker has a slow delivery in flight (e.g. codex turn/steer awaiting its RPC round-trip); orchestrator calls interrupt(w) (status 'stopping') and another send(w, msg) queues behind the in-flight delivery; the interrupt confirms and finalizes (task 'cancelled', worker 'idle') before the queued slot opens; the queued send then passes the stopping guard, delivers msg to the live session, the worker runs a fresh turn, and on turn_completed the trust gate flips the user-cancelled task to 'completed' — the caller of send() was told ok:true and the cancellation is silently undone.

title: Dup-session guard is no longer atomic: the new await on worktreeReady lets two racing spawns for one worker create two children, leaking one unmanaged process
claim: In all three session adapters the one-active-session-per-worker guard reads this._sessions BEFORE the newly-introduced `await opts.worktreeReady`, while this._sessions.set happens after it; the await opened a suspension window (pre-change the guard-to-set path was fully synchronous) during which a second spawn for the same worker also passes the guard, so both spawn OS children and the second sessions.set clobbers the first — the first child keeps running and emitting events under the same worker id (duplicate lifecycle.spawned, interleaved turn lifecycle breaking one-start/one-terminal accounting) and can never be reached by kill()/interrupt(), which only consult the map.
evidence: claude-session.mjs:122-125 (guard) vs :132 (await) vs :180 (sessions.set); codex-appserver.mjs:374-377 vs :385 vs :409; grok-acp.mjs:401-404 vs :411 vs :436. Pre-image (git show b85c58d^) shows no await between guard and set in any of the three. Empirically reproduced (scratch): two spawn('w1',...) calls sharing a pending worktreeReady both returned {ok:true}, two lifecycle.spawned events with two distinct pids, one map entry — kill('w1') reaches only the mapped pid.
failureScenario: A direct API caller (SC2 exports these classes as product surface) double-fires spawn(worker, brief, {worktreeReady}) — e.g. a retry while the worktree promise is still pending. Both calls pass the guard, two real CLI processes start in the worktree, both stream events as the same worker (the trust gate and story see doubled turn completions), and the unmapped child survives kill() indefinitely, burning real quota.

title: worktreeReady resolving after a forced stop spawns a live, unmanaged worker for a dead handle
claim: spawn() has no post-await recheck that the worker was killed while it waited on worktreeReady, and adapter.kill() on a not-yet-created session is a silent no-op ({ok:true} at claude-session.mjs:450, grok-acp.mjs:573); if the coordinator's stop deadline fires while the worktree promise is still pending, _forceStop's adapter.kill also no-ops, and when the worktree finally resolves the adapter proceeds to create a real child that runs the full brief for a worker whose handle is 'dead' — no trust gate (blocked by the 'dead' check), no kill path left, events logged post-mortem.
evidence: claude-session.mjs:129-136 (await with no abort recheck; sessions.set only at :180), :449-450 (kill no-ops without a session), coordinator.mjs:577-601 (_forceStop kills via adapter once, then deletes the waiter), :782 (dead handle blocks trust gate). Empirically reproduced (scratch repro-zombie): kill resolved 'forced', handle 'dead', then the late worktree resolution spawned pid alive:true and the dead worker's log gained lifecycle.turn_started/lifecycle.spawned/content.message/lifecycle.turn_completed.
failureScenario: On a repo where worktrees.create (git worktree add) outlasts stopDeadlineMs (15s default; large monorepos), the operator kills a just-dispatched task: forced stop marks the worker dead and its adapter.kill no-ops because no session exists yet; seconds later the worktree resolves, the adapter spawns a live claude/grok child that executes the entire brief unmanaged — the exact G1 zombie class SC1d was written to eliminate, now unkillable through the coordinator because every stop waiter is already consumed.

title: Codex turn/start-failure refusal leaves a live child and a non-terminal session that the SC1d consumer never reaps
claim: codex spawn()'s third failure leg (turn/start) returns {ok:false} without _killChild or sessions.delete — unlike the initialize and thread/start legs in the same function which do both — and the new SC1d consumer treats any {ok:false} as 'nothing is running' (logs lifecycle.crashed, marks handle 'exited', frees the slot) without ever calling adapter.kill; the still-running codex app-server process and its map entry are orphaned for the life of the host.
evidence: codex-appserver.mjs:447-449 (catch with no cleanup) vs :414-418 and :429-435 (both earlier legs _killChild + sessions.delete); coordinator.mjs:242-255 (_onSpawnRefused never invokes adapter.kill). The SC1d test (phase10-completion.test.mjs:198-205) stubs a clean refusal and never exercises codex's turn/start leg.
failureScenario: codex app-server completes initialize and thread/start but rejects turn/start (e.g. -32000 rate limit or a model-config error): the coordinator fails the task and moves on, but a live codex process with an idle thread persists indefinitely — nothing in the system will signal it (the coordinator never kills a spawn-refused worker), and repeated occurrences accumulate one leaked OS process per refused dispatch.

title: Narrative counts one worker as both active and done, and 'done (verified)' persists from a stale verdict after later work fails
claim: lastVerdict is never cleared on TURN_STARTED, so a worker running a second turn (coordinator send() -> new turn, redispatch explicitly anticipated by SC5c) is simultaneously counted in activeCount (status 'working') and doneCount (lastVerdict.accept === true), making the header report more worker-states than workers; and because a trust-gate exception logs kind 'error' (a no-op fold) instead of verify.reverified, the phrase for a worker whose later turn's verification errored permanently reads 'done (verified)' from the previous turn's verdict while the task is actually 'failed'.
evidence: story.mjs:319-325 (TURN_STARTED fold does not reset lastVerdict), :356-360 (only REVERIFIED writes it), :620-623 (activeCount/doneCount overlap), :572-575 (stale phrase); coordinator.mjs:903-914 (trust-gate failure logs kind 'error', story.mjs:416-417 folds it as no-op). Empirically reproduced (scratch): one worker rendered '1 worker(s) active, 1 done' during turn 2, and after turn 2's gate errored the narrative read '0 worker(s) active, 1 done / w1 (t1): done (verified)' for a failed task. Implementation matches SC5d's letter, so the defect lives in the contract's own mechanism — flagged because SC5d's stated goal is 'narrative truth'.
failureScenario: Worker completes turn 1, verify.reverified accept:true; orchestrator sends a follow-up message starting turn 2. Narrative header shows '1 worker(s) active, 1 done' with a single worker. Turn 2 completes but its trust gate throws (kind 'error' logged, no reverify event): the task is failed, yet the story permanently renders the worker as 'done (verified)' and counts it done — an operator reading the story believes the failed work was verified-accepted.
